text: A developer needs to initialise an Azure AI Foundry project client in Python using a connection string. Which method on AIProjectClient creates the client correctly?
options: AIProjectClient.create(credential=cred, conn_str=conn_str)
AIProjectClient.from_connection_string(credential=cred, conn_str=conn_str)
AIProjectClient.connect(credential=cred, endpoint=endpoint)
AIProjectClient.initialize(credential=cred, project_name=project)
expl:
Correct answer: B — AIProjectClient.from_connection_string().

The azure-ai-projects SDK uses the class method from_connection_string() to instantiate the client, passing a DefaultAzureCredential or other credential and the Foundry project connection string. create(), connect(), and initialize() are not valid class methods and will raise AttributeError.

text: An AI agent in Azure AI Foundry is configured with a retrieval tool and a function-calling tool. The agent consistently calls the function tool for every query — including ones clearly answerable from the vector index — adding unnecessary latency and API cost. Which configuration change resolves this without removing the function tool?
options: Set tool_choice='required' to force the agent to always use a tool on every turn
Set tool_choice='auto' so the agent decides which tool to call based on the query
Set temperature=0 to make the agent's tool selection deterministic
Remove the function tool from the toolset and re-register it only when needed
expl:
Correct answer: B — Set tool_choice='auto'.

tool_choice='auto' lets the model decide on each turn whether to call a tool and which tool to call based on the query context. If the query can be answered from the vector index, the agent will use retrieval; if it requires live data, it uses the function tool. tool_choice='required' forces a tool call every turn — worsening the problem. Temperature affects generation randomness, not tool selection logic. Dynamically removing and re-registering tools is an anti-pattern that requires recreating the agent.

text: A developer wants to send a message to an existing agent thread and create a run. Complete the blank to correctly create a user message on the thread.
code:
thread = client.agents.create_thread()

client.agents._____(  
    thread_id=thread.id,
    role="user",
    content="Summarise the Q3 financial report"
)

run = client.agents.create_and_process_run(
    thread_id=thread.id,
    agent_id=agent_id
)
options: add_message()
create_message()
send_message()
post_message()
expl:
Correct answer: C — create_message().

The azure-ai-projects SDK uses client.agents.create_message() to add a message to a thread. It accepts thread_id, role ("user" or "assistant"), and content. add_message(), send_message(), and post_message() are not valid method names and will raise AttributeError.

text: The following code retrieves the final agent response after a run completes but always raises an AttributeError. Identify the line causing this behaviour.
options: run = client.agents.create_and_process_run(...)
for msg in messages.items:
messages = client.agents.list_messages(thread_id=thread.id)
print(msg.content[0].text.value)
expl:
Correct answer: C — for msg in messages.items:

The list_messages() call returns a MessageList object where messages are stored in the .data attribute — not .items. Iterating over .items raises AttributeError because that attribute does not exist on MessageList. The correct pattern is: for msg in messages.data. The run creation, list_messages call, and content access are all correct.

text: A developer is configuring an Azure AI Foundry agent with the code interpreter tool. They want to pre-load two reference CSV files that the agent can use across all conversation sessions without re-uploading each time. Which TWO steps are required? (Select TWO)
options: Upload each CSV using client.agents.upload_file_and_poll() to obtain a file_id for each file
Store the CSV files in Azure Blob Storage and include the SAS URLs in each user message
Register the CSV files as Foundry data assets — the code interpreter accesses all registered data assets automatically
Attach the file_ids to the agent at creation time in the tool_resources for the code_interpreter tool
expl:
Correct answers: A and D

Pre-loading files for the code interpreter requires: (1) uploading each file using upload_file_and_poll() which returns a persistent file_id, and (2) attaching those file_ids to the agent at creation in tool_resources: {"code_interpreter": {"file_ids": [file_id_1, file_id_2]}}. SAS URLs in messages (B) require re-downloading each turn. Data assets (C) are not automatically accessible to the code interpreter without explicit file attachment.

text: Match each Azure AI Foundry agent memory type to its correct scope and persistence behaviour.
slots: Persists within a single conversation session only — cleared when session ends
Persists across separate sessions for a specific user — survives session resets
Static context defined at agent creation — same for all users and sessions
Retrieves relevant past context from a vector store on each turn
expl:
Correct matches: Thread memory → single session | Cross-session → across sessions | System prompt → static/all users | RAG memory → vector retrieval per turn.

These four memory types represent distinct scopes in AI-103 agent design. Thread memory is the default per-conversation history. Cross-session memory requires a persistent store (e.g. Cosmos DB) keyed to a user identifier. System prompt memory is static and identical for every user. Retrieval-augmented memory dynamically fetches relevant context from a vector index on each turn.

text: An AI agent used for automated loan approval decisions in the EU must comply with the EU AI Act. A lawyer asks: at what stage must a conformity assessment be completed? Which answer is correct?
options: Before placing the high-risk AI system on the market or putting it into service
After go-live — the system can launch and the conformity assessment is completed within 12 months of deployment
Conformity assessment is only required if the system causes harm — it is triggered reactively
Conformity assessment applies only to AI systems that use biometric data — loan approval systems are exempt
expl:
Correct answer: A — Before placing the system on the market or putting it into service.

The EU AI Act requires that high-risk AI systems (which include automated loan/credit decisions) must complete a conformity assessment before deployment — not after go-live. Conformity assessment is proactive, not reactive. The biometric exemption claim is false — loan and credit scoring systems are explicitly listed as high-risk in Annex III of the EU AI Act.

text: A developer is building a multi-agent solution where a coordinator agent must invoke a specialist summarisation agent. The specialist agent is already deployed in Azure AI Foundry. Which pattern correctly implements agent-to-agent invocation?
options: Deploy both agents behind Azure API Management and use APIM policies to route between them based on query content

Configure both agents to share the same conversation thread — the specialist agent reads coordinator messages and responds automatically. This option outlines a possible implementation detail for the AI solution.
Use Azure Service Bus to publish coordinator outputs as messages — the specialist agent subscribes and processes them
Register the specialist agent's run API as a function tool on the coordinator — when the coordinator emits a tool_call, the application executes a run on the specialist agent and returns its response
expl:
Correct answer: D — Register specialist agent as a function tool on the coordinator.

The correct AI-103 multi-agent pattern is to wrap the specialist agent's invocation (create_thread, create_message, create_and_process_run, retrieve response) as a Python function and register it as a function tool on the coordinator. When the coordinator decides to delegate, it emits a tool_call, the application executes the specialist agent run, and returns the response to the coordinator thread. Shared threads cause agents to interfere with each other's reasoning. Service Bus and APIM add infrastructure complexity without Foundry-native integration.

text: A developer is implementing streaming for an Azure AI Foundry agent run so the user sees tokens progressively. Complete the blank to use the correct streaming method.
options: run_stream()
stream_run()
create_streaming_run()
create_run_stream()
expl:
Correct answer: A — create_run_stream().

The azure-ai-projects SDK provides create_run_stream() as a context manager that yields streaming events during agent execution. It is the correct method for progressive token rendering. stream_run(), create_streaming_run(), and run_stream() are not valid SDK method names.

text: A developer is using Azure AI Foundry Content Understanding to process customer call recordings. The output schema requires: speaker_label, timestamp_start, timestamp_end, and transcript per segment. Which Content Understanding configuration produces this structured output?
options: Use Azure AI Speech batch transcription and post-process the VTT output with a custom parser to extract speaker labels and timestamps
Configure an audio analyzer with a custom output schema defining the four required fields — Content Understanding returns structured JSON matching the schema
Use the Document Intelligence read model — it supports audio inputs when configured with the speech modality flag
Configure a Prompt Flow with an Azure AI Speech step followed by a GPT-4o step that structures the transcript into the required JSON schema
expl:
Correct answer: B — Content Understanding audio analyzer with custom output schema.

Content Understanding in Azure AI Foundry supports audio as an input modality and allows you to define a custom output schema (JSON) specifying the exact fields you want extracted — including speaker_label, timestamps, and transcript per segment. It returns typed, structured JSON directly. Speech batch transcription (A) returns raw VTT/JSON that requires custom parsing. Document Intelligence (C) does not support audio inputs. Prompt Flow (D) achieves the result but requires two services and custom orchestration when Content Understanding handles it natively.

text: An Azure AI Foundry vector index backed by Azure AI Search is returning stale results after source documents in Blob Storage were updated 2 hours ago. The indexer is on a PT30M schedule. What is the most likely cause and correct resolution?
options: The vector index does not support incremental updates — the entire index must be rebuilt from scratch after any document change
Blob Storage change detection requires an Azure Event Grid subscription — without it, the indexer cannot detect updated files
The embedding model has cached the old document vectors — clear the embedding cache in the Foundry project settings
The indexer has not yet run since the document was updated — wait for the next scheduled run or trigger the indexer manually via the Run API
expl:
Correct answer: D — Wait for the next scheduled run or trigger manually.

Azure AI Search indexers poll for changes on their configured schedule. With PT30M scheduling, updates can take up to 30 minutes to appear. If immediate consistency is needed, the indexer can be triggered via the Run API or the Azure portal. Vector indexes support incremental updates — full rebuilds are not required. There is no embedding cache to clear. Event Grid is optional for faster triggering but not required for basic change detection with Blob Storage indexers.

text: A Foundry agent must never respond with content that could be considered harmful, and all agent responses must be evaluated for safety before reaching users in production. Which TWO mechanisms implement this defence-in-depth approach? (Select TWO)
options: Use Azure API Management rate limiting to throttle requests — reducing request volume reduces the probability of harmful outputs
Configure Azure OpenAI content filters on the model deployment — harmful content categories are blocked at the infrastructure level before the response leaves the model
Run Azure AI Evaluation SDK safety evaluators (SelfHarmEvaluator, HateUnfairnessEvaluator) on a representative dataset before production release to measure risk
Set the agent's system prompt to 'Never generate harmful content' — this is sufficient as the primary safety control
expl:
Correct answers: B and C

Defence-in-depth for safety requires: (1) content filters on the Azure OpenAI deployment (B) — these operate at infrastructure level and block harmful categories on every response automatically, and (2) pre-production safety evaluation using the Evaluation SDK (C) — this measures the probability and severity of harmful outputs before going live. A system prompt instruction (D) alone is not a reliable safety control — it can be bypassed. Rate limiting (A) is a performance/cost control, not a safety mechanism.

scen: A logistics company is building an AI-103 solution on Azure AI Foundry. The solution processes shipping manifests (PDFs), customer complaint emails, and real-time package tracking updates from an internal API. An AI agent must: answer customer queries about shipment status, flag high-urgency complaints for human review, and generate weekly delay analysis reports. All data must remain within the company's Azure subscription.
text: The solution must extract structured fields (tracking number, origin, destination, estimated delivery date, item count) from 6 different PDF manifest templates. No prebuilt Document Intelligence model covers this format. The team has 40 labeled samples per template. Which approach is most appropriate?
options: Train a custom Document Intelligence extraction model per template using the 40 labeled samples, then compose all 6 into a composed model
Use the prebuilt Document Intelligence invoice model — it supports custom field names via configuration without training
Use Azure AI Foundry Content Understanding with a document schema — no labeled training samples are required
Use a GPT-4o multimodal deployment — submit each manifest page as an image and extract fields via a structured JSON prompt
expl:
Correct answer: A — Custom Document Intelligence models composed.

With 6 distinct templates, no prebuilt coverage, and 40 labeled samples per template (exceeding the minimum 5), custom extraction models trained per template and composed under a single endpoint is the correct approach. The prebuilt invoice model (B) is for invoice-specific fields — it cannot be configured for arbitrary field names without training. Content Understanding (C) is powerful for unstructured content but less precise for fixed-field extraction across known templates. GPT-4o (D) is non-deterministic and expensive at logistics scale.

text: The AI agent must retrieve real-time package tracking status from the internal API and answer customer queries. The API requires an OAuth 2.0 client credentials token. Where should the token acquisition logic be implemented?
options: In the agent's system prompt — include the bearer token so the model passes it in tool call arguments
In the Azure AI Foundry agent configuration — add the OAuth token as a connection credential in the project settings
In the function tool implementation — the Python function acquires the token using client credentials flow and attaches it to the API request
In the user message — the client application acquires the token and passes it with each user query
expl:
Correct answer: C — In the function tool implementation.

Authentication to external APIs is always handled inside the function tool's Python implementation — not by the model, the agent config, or the client application. The function acquires a token using client credentials flow (e.g. via MSAL or DefaultAzureCredential with the right scope), attaches it as a Bearer token to the API request, and returns structured results to the agent. Putting the token in the system prompt (A) exposes it in traces and responses. Foundry agent connections (B) are for Azure service connections, not arbitrary OAuth flows. Passing the token in user messages (D) exposes credentials in conversation history.

text: The logistics solution has several processing requirements. Match each requirement to the correct Azure AI service or Foundry feature.
items: Extract structured fields from 6 PDF manifest templates
Analyse customer complaint emails for urgency and sentiment
Transcribe voicemail complaints (up to 5 minutes long)
Answer customer queries about shipment status using agent + vector index
slots: Azure AI Document Intelligence — custom composed model
Azure AI Language — sentiment analysis + NER
Azure AI Foundry — Agents Service with retrieval tool
expl:
Correct matches: PDF manifests → Document Intelligence custom composed | Email analysis → AI Language sentiment + NER | Voicemail → Speech batch transcription | Customer queries → Foundry Agents with retrieval.

Each maps to the purpose-built AI-103 service for that modality: Document Intelligence for structured PDF extraction, AI Language for text sentiment and entity recognition, Speech batch transcription for asynchronous long audio files, and Foundry Agents with a retrieval tool for grounded Q&A over indexed shipment data.

text: The solution must ensure all data remains within the company's Azure subscription — no data must traverse the public internet. Which TWO configurations are required? (Select TWO)
options: Configure Azure Private Endpoints for all Azure AI services and the Foundry project, disabling public network access
Deploy all application components in an Azure Virtual Network and route AI service traffic through the VNet via service endpoints or private endpoints
Enable encryption at rest on all Azure AI service resources — this prevents data from leaving the subscription
Use Azure API Management to proxy all AI service calls — APIM keeps traffic private by default
expl:
Correct answers: A and B

Private Endpoints (A) create private IP addresses for Azure AI services inside the company's network, disabling public access. VNet integration (B) routes application traffic to AI services through private network paths. Together they ensure end-to-end private connectivity. API Management (D) proxies HTTP traffic but does not inherently keep it private — it would also need private endpoint configuration. Encryption at rest (C) protects stored data — it does not control network routing or prevent data from traversing the public internet.

text: A developer is configuring Azure AI Foundry Prompt Flow for a RAG pipeline. The flow has three nodes: embed_query, vector_search, and llm_response. During testing, the llm_response node receives an empty context and generates a hallucinated answer. The embed_query and vector_search nodes complete successfully. What is the most likely cause?
options: The embedding model is returning zero-length vectors — the vector search returns no results
The system prompt in llm_response does not instruct the model to use the context — it answers from training data by default
The LLM deployment referenced in llm_response is not deployed in the same Foundry project as the flow
The output of the vector_search node is not correctly wired as the input to the llm_response node in the flow's DAG configuration
expl:
Correct answer: D — vector_search output not wired to llm_response input.

In Prompt Flow's DAG (directed acyclic graph), node outputs must be explicitly connected to downstream node inputs. If vector_search completes successfully but llm_response receives empty context, the most likely cause is that the connection between nodes is missing or misconfigured — the context variable is not mapped from vector_search output to llm_response input. Zero-length vectors would cause vector_search to fail, not succeed. A different project deployment would cause an authentication error. System prompt grounding is a separate concern — the node still receives whatever is wired to its context input.

text: An organisation is deploying a Foundry agent for HR query handling. The agent sometimes provides incorrect information about parental leave policies for employees in specific countries. The HR team wants to measure and mitigate this. Which evaluation metric most directly measures this risk?
options: Coherence score — measures whether the agent's response logically follows from the question
Fluency score — measures the grammatical quality and naturalness of the agent's response
Groundedness score — measures whether the agent's response is supported by the retrieved policy documents
Relevance score — measures whether the agent's response addresses the employee's question
expl:
Correct answer: C — Groundedness score.

Groundedness directly measures whether the agent's claims are supported by the retrieved context (policy documents). Low groundedness = the agent is making claims not present in the retrieved policies = incorrect information risk. Coherence measures logical flow — not factual accuracy. Fluency measures grammar — not content correctness. Relevance measures whether the answer addresses the question — a response can be relevant but still factually wrong if it hallucates.

text: A developer is implementing a function tool that calls an external REST API and returns results to the Foundry agent. Complete the blank so the function is correctly registered with the agent using FunctionTool.
code:
import json
import requests
from azure.ai.projects.models import FunctionTool, ToolSet

def get_shipment_status(tracking_number: str) -> str:
    response = requests.get(
        f"https://api.logistics.internal/track/{tracking_number}",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {acquire_token()}"}
    )
    return json.dumps(response.json())

functions = FunctionTool(functions=_____)
toolset = ToolSet()
toolset.add(functions)

agent = client.agents.create_agent(
    model="gpt-4o",
    name="logistics-agent",
    instructions="You are a logistics assistant.",
    toolset=toolset
)
options: [get_shipment_status]
(get_shipment_status,)
{get_shipment_status}
get_shipment_status
expl:
Correct answer: B — {get_shipment_status}.

FunctionTool expects a Python set of function references — not a list, tuple, or single function. Using {get_shipment_status} (a set containing the function) is the correct syntax. A list [get_shipment_status] and a tuple (get_shipment_status,) are not valid — the SDK specifically expects a set. Passing the function directly without a container raises a TypeError.

text: A production Foundry agent has been running for 3 months. The team wants to identify which tool calls are taking the longest and causing high latency for users. Which Azure AI Foundry feature provides per-step timing data for each agent run?
options: Azure Monitor Metrics — configure latency metrics on the Azure OpenAI resource to measure token generation time
Azure AI Evaluation SDK — run a latency evaluator on a sample of past conversations
Azure Application Insights — instrument the application to log timestamps before and after each agent turn
Azure AI Foundry Tracing — each agent run trace includes per-step timing, tool call durations, and end-to-end latency
expl:
Correct answer: D — Azure AI Foundry Tracing.

Foundry Tracing captures full OpenTelemetry traces for every agent run — each span includes start time, end time, and duration for every step: LLM calls, tool invocations, retrieval operations, and the overall run. This makes it the correct tool for diagnosing per-step latency. Azure Monitor Metrics (A) measures aggregate resource-level metrics — not per-step agent execution timing. Application Insights (C) requires manual timestamp instrumentation. The Evaluation SDK (B) measures quality metrics — it does not evaluate latency.

text: Arrange the following steps in the correct order for implementing an agentic RAG workflow in Azure AI Foundry from scratch.
items: Chunk source documents and generate embeddings using an embedding model deployment
Define the agent's system prompt with grounding instructions
Create an Azure AI Search index with a vector field and populate it with embedded chunks
Create the Foundry agent and attach the retrieval tool pointing to the vector index
Test the agent in Foundry Playground and run groundedness evaluation
expl:
Correct order: (1) Chunk and embed source documents → (2) Create AI Search index and populate with embeddings → (3) Define agent system prompt → (4) Create agent with retrieval tool → (5) Test and evaluate.

The data pipeline must exist before the agent can query it. Chunking and embedding comes first, then index creation and population, then agent design (system prompt), then wiring the retrieval tool, and finally testing and evaluation before production.

text: A developer deploys a GPT-4o model in Azure AI Foundry and calls it using the azure-ai-inference SDK. The call returns a 404 error. The endpoint URL and API version are confirmed correct. What is the most likely cause?
options: The azure-ai-inference SDK requires a different API version than the one used for the Azure OpenAI SDK
GPT-4o is not supported by the azure-ai-inference SDK — it requires the AzureOpenAI client from the openai package
The model parameter passed to the client.complete() call does not match the deployment name in the Foundry project
The DefaultAzureCredential does not work with the azure-ai-inference SDK — an API key must be used
expl:
Correct answer: C — Model parameter does not match the deployment name.

In Azure AI Foundry, models are accessed by their deployment name — not the base model name. Passing model='gpt-4o' when the deployment is named 'my-gpt4o-prod' results in a 404 because no deployment with that exact name exists. The fix is to use the exact deployment name. The azure-ai-inference SDK supports GPT-4o and works with DefaultAzureCredential — both A and D are incorrect. API version differences do not typically cause 404 errors.

text: The following code runs a parallel tool call workflow — the agent emits two tool calls simultaneously and the application submits both results. The code runs but only the first tool result is visible to the agent. Identify the bug.
options: tool_calls = run.required_action.submit_tool_outputs.tool_calls
output = execute_tool(tc.function.name, tc.function.arguments)
results.append({"tool_call_id": tc.id, "output": output})
client.agents.submit_tool_outputs_to_run(..., tool_outputs=results[0])
expl:
Correct answer: C — tool_outputs=results[0].

results[0] submits only the first tool result to the run. The tool_outputs parameter must receive the complete list of all tool results — tool_outputs=results. The agent requires all pending tool outputs to be submitted in a single call before it can continue reasoning. Submitting only the first one leaves the second tool call unresolved and the agent cannot proceed past the tool call step.

text: Microsoft's Responsible AI principle of Transparency requires which of the following in an AI-103 solution?
options: The AI system must make decisions that are statistically fair across all demographic groups it affects
People must be informed when they are interacting with an AI system and must be able to understand how it makes decisions
The AI system must be reliable under a wide range of conditions including adversarial inputs
The AI system must protect users' personal data and respect their privacy throughout its operation
expl:
Correct answer: B — People must be informed they are interacting with AI and understand how decisions are made.

Transparency in Microsoft's Responsible AI framework means: disclosing that a system is AI-powered, making the system's purpose and capabilities understandable, and enabling meaningful explanation of decisions. Fairness (A) is a separate principle. Reliability and Safety (C) is a separate principle. Privacy and Security (D) is a separate principle. Each of the six principles is distinct and commonly tested as a matching exercise on AI-103.

text: An organisation has an existing Azure AI Search index used for keyword search. They want to add vector similarity search without re-indexing all documents from scratch. Which is the most efficient approach?
options: Delete the existing index and rebuild it with a vector field — incremental addition of vector fields to existing indexes is not supported
Enable semantic ranker on the existing index — semantic ranker provides vector-like similarity search without adding a vector field
Create a second separate vector index and merge results from both indexes in the application layer using a custom RRF implementation
Add a vector field to the existing index schema, run a custom skill to generate embeddings for existing documents, and run the indexer to populate the new field
expl:
Correct answer: D — Add a vector field and run an embedding skill.

Azure AI Search supports adding new fields to an existing index schema without deleting it. Adding a vector field (Collection(Edm.Single) with dimensions and vectorSearchProfile), then running an indexer with an embedding skill (e.g. AzureOpenAIEmbeddingSkill) populates the new field for existing documents. Full rebuild (A) is unnecessary. A separate index (C) adds complexity without leveraging the existing index's keyword search for hybrid. Semantic ranker (B) re-ranks keyword results using language models — it does not perform vector similarity search and does not require a vector field.

text: A developer wants to evaluate an AI-103 RAG agent across three quality dimensions simultaneously: whether responses are grounded in context, whether they are relevant to the question, and whether they are coherent. Which TWO statements about running this evaluation are correct? (Select TWO)
options: Each evaluator must be run in a separate evaluate() call — multiple evaluators cannot share the same dataset in one call
All three evaluators (GroundednessEvaluator, RelevanceEvaluator, CoherenceEvaluator) can be passed together in the evaluators dict of a single evaluate() call
The JSONL evaluation dataset must include 'query', 'response', and 'context' fields to satisfy all three evaluators
Groundedness evaluation does not require a 'context' field — it evaluates the response text alone against the model's internal knowledge
expl:
Correct answers: B and C

The evaluate() function accepts multiple evaluators in a single call via the evaluators dict — e.g. evaluators={'groundedness': g_eval, 'relevance': r_eval, 'coherence': c_eval}. All evaluators run against the same dataset in one call (B). The JSONL dataset must include query, response, and context fields (C) — groundedness requires context to measure whether the response is supported by retrieved content (D is false — groundedness specifically needs context, not just the response).

text: A developer is running a safety evaluation using the Azure AI Evaluation SDK. Complete the blank to correctly pass the Azure AI project details required to log results to Foundry.
code:
from azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, HateUnfairnessEvaluator
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential

evaluator = HateUnfairnessEvaluator(
    _____={
        "subscription_id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
        "resource_group_name": "my-rg",
        "project_name": "my-foundry-project"
    },
    credential=DefaultAzureCredential()
)

results = evaluate(
    data="safety_eval.jsonl",
    evaluators={"hate": evaluator},
    output_path="results.json"
)
options: project
foundry_project
azure_ai_project
ai_project
expl:
Correct answer: B — azure_ai_project.

The safety evaluator constructors in the azure-ai-evaluation SDK use the parameter name azure_ai_project to receive the project connection details dict (subscription_id, resource_group_name, project_name). project, foundry_project, and ai_project are not valid parameter names and will raise a TypeError.

text: A Foundry agent is configured with human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval for high-value actions. During a run, the agent reaches a HITL checkpoint. What status does the run enter while awaiting human approval, and how does the application detect this?
options: The run status changes to 'paused' — the application polls get_run() and checks for status=='paused'
The run status changes to 'requires_action' with action type 'submit_tool_outputs' — the application polls get_run() and handles the pending approval
The run emits a webhook notification to the application's callback URL — no polling is required. This option outlines a possible implementation detail for the AI solution.
The run status changes to 'waiting' — the application checks run.waiting_for in the response object
expl:
Correct answer: B — Status changes to 'requires_action'.

When a Foundry agent run reaches a point requiring external input (including HITL approval checkpoints), the run status transitions to 'requires_action'. The application detects this by polling client.agents.get_run() and checking run.status == 'requires_action', then inspecting run.required_action to determine the type of action needed. 'paused' and 'waiting' are not valid run status values. Webhook callbacks are not the native notification mechanism — polling is the correct pattern.

text: A developer is building a Prompt Flow in Azure AI Foundry that calls a GPT-4o deployment and a custom Python function. The flow must be deployed as a real-time REST endpoint that auto-scales between 1 and 10 instances based on request volume. Which deployment option is correct?
options: Batch Endpoint — supports auto-scaling and is the recommended deployment target for real-time Prompt Flow APIs
Managed Online Endpoint — deploys the flow as a REST endpoint on Foundry-managed compute with configurable auto-scaling
Azure Functions — package the flow as a serverless function with HTTP trigger and consumption-based scaling
Azure Container Apps — containerise the flow and configure KEDA-based HTTP scaling rules
expl:
Correct answer: B — Managed Online Endpoint.

Managed Online Endpoints are the native deployment target for real-time Prompt Flow inference in Azure AI Foundry — they expose a REST endpoint, manage compute provisioning, and support auto-scaling configuration (min/max instances, scale-out triggers). Batch Endpoints process large offline batches, not real-time requests. Azure Functions and Container Apps can host flows but require custom packaging and are not native Foundry deployment targets.

text: Match each Azure AI Foundry / AI-103 component to its correct primary function.
slots: Shared infrastructure layer — connections, compute, security policies shared across projects
Developer workspace — models, agents, flows, evaluations for a specific solution
Orchestration tool for building and deploying LLM-based pipelines as DAG flows
Programmatic framework for measuring AI quality and safety metrics
expl:
Correct matches: Hub → shared infrastructure | Project → developer workspace | Prompt Flow → DAG-based pipeline orchestration | Evaluation SDK → quality/safety measurement.

The Hub/Project hierarchy separates shared enterprise infrastructure from team-specific workspaces. Prompt Flow is the visual and code-based DAG orchestration tool for building LLM pipelines. The Evaluation SDK provides evaluators (groundedness, safety, coherence, relevance) that run programmatically against datasets.

text: An AI-103 content moderation agent incorrectly flags posts from users of a specific language community at 3x the rate of other communities. Which TWO Responsible AI actions address this issue? (Select TWO)
options: Increase the content filter severity threshold to reduce overall flagging volume — this will proportionally reduce false positives for all groups
Deploy a separate content moderation model per language community — this eliminates cross-community comparison
Run HateUnfairnessEvaluator on a dataset stratified by language community to measure whether error rates differ significantly across groups
Audit the training data or evaluation dataset for representation imbalance across language communities and address gaps
expl:
Correct answers: C and D

The issue is a Fairness violation — differential error rates across demographic/community groups. The correct actions are: (1) measure the disparity systematically using a stratified evaluation dataset and the HateUnfairnessEvaluator (C), and (2) audit and address representation imbalance in the data (D) — skewed training or evaluation data is a common root cause of differential performance. Raising the threshold (A) reduces overall volume but does not address the relative disparity — the 3x ratio may persist. Separate models per community (B) avoids the problem rather than solving it and creates maintenance overhead.

text: The following code creates an AI agent with a vector index retrieval tool in Azure AI Foundry. The agent is created successfully but never retrieves from the index — it always answers from its own knowledge. Identify the bug.
options: instructions="Answer HR questions using the provided context only."
tool_resources={"azure_ai_search": {"indexes": [...]}}
tools=[{"type": "azure_ai_search"}]
tool_choice="auto"
expl:
Correct answer: A — tools=[{"type": "azure_ai_search"}].

The tool type string for the Azure AI Search retrieval tool in the Foundry agents API is "file_search" or the Foundry-specific retrieval tool type — not "azure_ai_search". Using an unrecognised tool type string means the tool is not registered correctly, so the agent has no retrieval capability despite tool_resources being configured. The tool_resources, instructions, and tool_choice are all correctly set. The fix is to use the correct tool type string as specified in the current Foundry agents API documentation.

text: A developer needs to implement iterative agentic RAG — the agent queries the vector index, evaluates whether the retrieved content is sufficient, and if not, reformulates the query and retrieves again before generating a final answer. Which agent capability enables this self-directed iteration?
options: Parallel tool calling — run multiple vector searches simultaneously and merge results before generation
Semantic ranker — Azure AI Search automatically refines query terms based on initial result scores
The agentic loop — on each turn the model decides whether to call the retrieval tool again with a refined query or generate a final answer
Chain-of-thought system prompt — instruct the model to reason before searching, which improves first-retrieval accuracy
expl:
Correct answer: C — The agentic loop.

The agentic loop is the core pattern enabling iterative RAG. On each turn the model evaluates its current context and decides: call the retrieval tool again with a refined query, or generate a final answer. This self-directed iteration is what distinguishes agentic RAG from single-turn RAG. Parallel tool calling runs concurrent searches — not sequential self-evaluating iterations. Semantic ranker refines within a single search call. Chain-of-thought improves reasoning quality but does not drive tool invocation decisions across turns.

text: A Foundry agent is processing a complex query and the run remains in 'in_progress' status for over 10 minutes without completing. The developer needs to cancel the run. Which SDK call cancels an in-progress agent run?
options: client.agents.delete_run(thread_id=thread_id, run_id=run_id)
client.agents.cancel_run(thread_id=thread_id, run_id=run_id)
client.agents.stop_run(thread_id=thread_id, run_id=run_id)
client.agents.terminate_run(thread_id=thread_id, run_id=run_id)
expl:
Correct answer: B — client.agents.cancel_run().

The azure-ai-projects SDK provides cancel_run() to request cancellation of an in-progress run. The run transitions to 'cancelling' and then 'cancelled' status. delete_run() removes the run record — it does not cancel an in-progress execution. stop_run() and terminate_run() are not valid SDK method names.

text: A developer is configuring Content Understanding in Azure AI Foundry to process product images and return structured output including product_name, colour, condition (new/used/damaged), and a damage_description field that is only populated when condition is 'damaged'. Which feature of Content Understanding schemas enables conditional field population?
options: Required field constraints — mark damage_description as required only when condition='damaged'
Optional fields with null default — define damage_description as an optional field; the model populates it only when relevant evidence is present in the image
Conditional schema logic — Content Understanding schemas support if-then conditions on field population
Post-processing rules — configure a Prompt Flow step after Content Understanding to null out damage_description when condition is not 'damaged'
expl:
Correct answer: B — Optional field with null default.

Content Understanding schemas support optional fields — when a field is defined as optional, the model only populates it when the relevant evidence exists in the input. For damage_description, defining it as optional means the model naturally populates it only when the image shows damage signs. Conditional schema logic with if-then conditions (B) is not a supported Content Understanding schema feature. Required field constraints (A) cannot depend on another field's value. A Prompt Flow post-processing step (D) achieves the same result but adds unnecessary orchestration complexity.

text: An organisation wants to implement AI agent observability in production — tracking which user queries trigger the most tool calls, which tools have the highest failure rate, and the average latency per tool type. Which combination of Azure services provides this analytics capability?
options: Azure Application Insights — instrument each tool function with custom events and metrics for per-tool analytics
Azure AI Foundry Tracing connected to Azure Monitor Log Analytics — traces are exported as structured logs and queried with KQL for tool-level analytics
Azure AI Evaluation SDK — run a tool-usage evaluator on a sample of past traces to compute tool call statistics
Azure Cost Management — tool call frequency correlates with API costs and can be used as a proxy for tool usage patterns
expl:
Correct answer: B — Foundry Tracing → Azure Monitor Log Analytics + KQL.

Foundry Tracing exports OpenTelemetry traces to Azure Monitor Log Analytics. Each trace span represents a step (LLM call, tool call, retrieval) with timing and status. KQL queries can aggregate tool call frequency, failure rates, and latency by tool type across all production runs. Application Insights (A) requires manual custom event instrumentation for each tool. The Evaluation SDK (C) measures quality metrics, not operational tool usage statistics. Cost Management (D) provides billing data — not tool-level execution analytics.

text: Match each AI-103 evaluation metric to its correct definition.
slots: Measures whether response claims are supported by the provided context
Measures whether the response is logically consistent and does not contradict itself
Measures whether the response addresses the user's question
Measures the grammatical quality and natural language fluency of the response
expl:
Correct matches: Groundedness → supported by context | Coherence → logically consistent | Relevance → addresses the question | Fluency → grammatical quality.

These four are the core quality evaluators in the azure-ai-evaluation SDK. Each measures a distinct dimension of response quality. Groundedness is the primary RAG-specific metric — it catches hallucinations. Coherence measures internal logical consistency. Relevance measures topical alignment with the query. Fluency measures surface-level language quality.

text: A developer needs to delete an Azure AI Foundry agent and all its associated threads and files when a customer account is deactivated. Which sequence of SDK calls achieves complete cleanup?
options: client.agents.delete_agent(agent_id) — this cascade-deletes all threads, messages, and files associated with the agent. This option outlines a possible implementation detail for the AI solution.
Delete each thread using client.agents.delete_thread(thread_id), delete each file using client.agents.delete_file(file_id), then delete the agent using client.agents.delete_agent(agent_id)
client.projects.delete_resources(agent_id) — Foundry project resource deletion handles all associated assets
Delete the Foundry project — all agents, threads, and files are deleted as part of project deletion
expl:
Correct answer: B — Delete threads and files individually, then delete the agent.

The Foundry agents API does not cascade-delete threads and files when an agent is deleted. Complete cleanup requires: (1) listing and deleting each thread with delete_thread(), (2) listing and deleting each file with delete_file(), then (3) deleting the agent with delete_agent(). Deleting only the agent leaves orphaned threads and files consuming storage. Project-level deletion (D) is a destructive operation affecting all resources in the project — not appropriate for single-customer cleanup.

text: An AI system used in a hospital to prioritise patient appointment scheduling is being assessed under the EU AI Act. Which risk category applies and what is the primary deployment obligation?
options: High risk — the system must complete a conformity assessment and implement human oversight before deployment
Limited risk — the system must display a transparency notice to patients informing them AI is used
Minimal risk — healthcare scheduling is an administrative function exempt from EU AI Act obligations
Unacceptable risk — AI systems that affect healthcare resource allocation are prohibited under the EU AI Act
expl:
Correct answer: A — High risk.

The EU AI Act Annex III explicitly lists AI systems used in healthcare resource allocation and prioritisation as high-risk. High-risk obligations include conformity assessment before deployment, human oversight capability, logging and audit trails, and registration in the EU AI database. It is not minimal risk — healthcare prioritisation directly affects patient welfare. Limited risk applies to chatbots and deepfakes. It is not prohibited — unacceptable risk is reserved for social scoring, real-time public biometric surveillance, and manipulation systems.

text: A developer is configuring a vector search query using the azure-ai-inference SDK's EmbeddingsClient. Complete the blank to correctly call the embedding generation method.

from azure.ai.inference import EmbeddingsClient
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential

vector = response.data[0].embedding
options: embed()

get_embeddings()

The EmbeddingsClient in the azure-ai-inference SDK uses the generate() method to create embeddings. It accepts an input list of strings and a model name (deployment name). The response.data[0].embedding returns the vector as a list of floats. embed(), encode(), and get_embeddings() are not valid method names on EmbeddingsClient.

text: A Foundry agent is being tested and the team notices that in some conversations the agent repeats the same tool call multiple times in a loop without making progress. This is known as a tool call loop. Which configuration prevents this?
options: Set temperature=0 — deterministic responses prevent the agent from making different tool call decisions each turn
Configure max_completion_tokens on the model deployment to limit the agent's response length. This choice reflects one way to configure the solution in Azure.
Set the run's max_iterations or max_steps parameter to limit the number of tool calls per run, combined with clear system prompt instructions to avoid repetition
Remove all tool definitions and use chain-of-thought prompting to simulate tool calls internally. It describes a common pattern that might be considered in this scenario.
expl:
Correct answer: C — max_iterations/max_steps combined with anti-repetition system prompt instructions.

Preventing tool call loops requires two complementary controls: (1) a hard limit on the number of agent turns/iterations per run (max_iterations or max_steps in the run configuration) as a safety ceiling, and (2) system prompt instructions telling the agent not to repeat tool calls if the previous result was insufficient — to either try a different approach or acknowledge inability to complete the task. Temperature=0 (A) makes output deterministic but does not break a loop pattern that is consistently reproduced. max_completion_tokens (B) limits response length, not the number of iterations.

text: A developer is building a document Q&A agent that must handle 3 document types: PDFs with embedded images, Excel spreadsheets, and PowerPoint presentations. The agent must be able to answer questions referencing content from any of these files. Which TWO capabilities should be combined for the ingestion pipeline? (Select TWO)
options: Azure AI Foundry Content Understanding — processes PDFs (including image content), Excel, and PowerPoint natively, generating structured text output for indexing
Azure AI Document Intelligence read model — handles all three file types with identical accuracy
Azure AI Search with a cognitive skillset including OCR skill, Excel extraction, and PowerPoint extraction skills — normalises all three formats to searchable text
A custom Azure Function that uses python-pptx, openpyxl, and PyMuPDF to extract text from each format and writes chunks to the index
expl:
Correct answers: A and C.

Content Understanding (A) natively supports multi-format document processing including PDFs with images, Excel, and PowerPoint — it generates structured output suitable for chunking and embedding in a RAG pipeline. Azure AI Search with a cognitive skillset (C) provides built-in extractors for Office formats and OCR for PDF images — all normalised to searchable text fields in the index. Document Intelligence read model (B) handles PDFs and images but does not support Excel or PowerPoint. A custom Azure Function (D) works but requires maintaining parsing libraries and adds development overhead when managed services provide the capability.

text: A Foundry project contains a GPT-4o deployment and a text-embedding-3-large deployment. A developer wants to use the azure-ai-inference SDK to call both from the same client endpoint. Which endpoint format is correct for the azure-ai-inference SDK with Azure AI Foundry?

https://{hub-name}.azureml.net/inference/ — the Azure Machine Learning inference endpoint
https://api.cognitive.microsoft.com/openai/ — the global Azure Cognitive Services endpoint
https://{project-name}.services.ai.azure.com/models — the Foundry project inference endpoint
expl:
Correct answer: D — https://{project-name}.services.ai.azure.com/models.

The azure-ai-inference SDK connects to Azure AI Foundry using the project-level inference endpoint in the format https://{project-name}.services.ai.azure.com/models. This single endpoint surfaces all model deployments in the project — both the GPT-4o and embedding deployments are accessible from the same client. The Azure OpenAI endpoint (A) is for the openai SDK pattern. The global Cognitive Services endpoint (C) is a legacy URL. The AzureML endpoint (B) is for custom model deployments on AML compute, not Foundry.

text: The following code configures a Foundry agent with a file search tool and uploads a policy document. The agent is created but the file search tool never finds content from the uploaded document. Identify the bug.
options: file = client.agents.upload_file_and_poll(file_path="hr_policy.pdf", purpose="assistants")
vector_store = client.agents.create_vector_store_and_poll(file_ids=[file.id], name="hr-policies")
tool_resources={"file_search": {"vector_store_ids": [file.id]}}
tools=[{"type": "file_search"}]
expl:
Correct answer: C — vector_store_ids contains file.id instead of vector_store.id.

The tool_resources for file_search must reference the vector store ID (vector_store.id), not the raw file ID (file.id). The file is uploaded and added to a vector store — the agent accesses files through the vector store, not directly by file ID. Passing file.id in vector_store_ids means the agent is looking for a vector store with an ID that matches a file ID — which does not exist. The fix is: "vector_store_ids": [vector_store.id].

text: A developer wants to test different system prompt configurations for a Foundry agent interactively — trying 4 different system messages against the same set of 10 test questions and comparing the responses side by side. Which Foundry tool is designed for this interactive comparison workflow with no code required?
options: Azure AI Evaluation SDK — run evaluate() four times with different system prompts and compare output JSON files
Azure AI Studio model catalog — the catalog comparison view shows side-by-side outputs for multiple model configurations
Prompt Flow — build a flow with 4 parallel LLM nodes, each with a different system prompt, and evaluate outputs
Foundry Playground — supports multi-configuration testing by creating multiple agent configurations and comparing responses interactively
expl:
Correct answer: D — Foundry Playground.

The Foundry Playground is the interactive no-code tool for testing and comparing model/agent configurations. It supports creating multiple system prompt configurations and running the same queries against them for direct response comparison. The Evaluation SDK (A) requires writing Python code. Prompt Flow (C) is a code/visual DAG tool — not designed for quick interactive comparisons. The model catalog (B) compares models, not system prompt configurations on the same model.

text: An organisation's AI agent generates customer-facing content. During evaluation, they find the agent produces inconsistent responses — giving different answers to the same question depending on minor phrasing variations. Which Responsible AI principle is most directly violated and what is the recommended mitigation?
options: Reliability and Safety — inconsistency is a reliability failure; reduce temperature, add system prompt consistency instructions, and test extensively across input variations
Fairness — inconsistent answers may disadvantage certain customer groups; add demographic fairness testing. The wording highlights a particular aspect of how the system could be set up.
Transparency — customers cannot understand why they receive different answers; add an explanation UI
Inclusiveness — inconsistency disproportionately affects users who phrase questions differently; expand training data diversity
expl:
Correct answer: A — Reliability and Safety.

Reliability is specifically about performing consistently and predictably under varied conditions. A system that gives different answers to the same question with minor phrasing changes is unreliable. Mitigations include: lowering temperature for more deterministic output, adding system prompt instructions for consistency, few-shot examples showing consistent response patterns, and robust testing across phrasing variations. Fairness (B) is about demographic group disparities. Transparency (C) is about explainability. Inclusiveness (D) is about accessibility for diverse user populations.

text: A Foundry agent run completes with status 'failed'. The developer needs to find the error details. Which property of the run object contains the failure reason?
options: run.error_message
run.failure_reason
run.status_details
run.last_error
expl:
Correct answer: D — run.last_error.

When an Azure AI Foundry agent run fails, the error details are available in run.last_error — a LastErrorDetails object containing a code and message field describing the failure reason. run.error_message, run.failure_reason, and run.status_details are not valid properties on the run object in the azure-ai-projects SDK.

text: A developer is submitting a multimodal message to a GPT-4o deployment using the azure-ai-inference SDK. The message contains an image (base64-encoded) and a text question. Complete the blank with the correct content item class for the image.
options: VisionContentItem
ImageMessage
ImageContentItem
Base64ContentItem
expl:
Correct answer: A — ImageContentItem.

In the azure-ai-inference SDK, multimodal user message content arrays use ImageContentItem for image inputs and TextContentItem for text inputs. ImageContentItem accepts an image_url parameter of type ImageUrl which holds the URL or base64 data URI. ImageMessage, VisionContentItem, and Base64ContentItem are not valid class names in this SDK.

text: A team is running a red-teaming exercise on their Foundry agent before production launch. Which TWO red-teaming scenarios are most relevant for an AI-103 agentic RAG solution? (Select TWO)
options: SQL injection via function tool parameters — the agent constructs SQL queries using user input without sanitisation
Prompt injection via retrieved documents — malicious content in indexed documents attempts to override the agent's instructions
Context window stuffing — a user submits an extremely long query to exceed the model's context window and trigger unpredictable behaviour
Cross-site scripting (XSS) via agent responses — the agent embeds JavaScript in HTML responses rendered by the client
expl:
Correct answers: B and C

For agentic RAG solutions, the two most AI-specific red-teaming scenarios are: (1) Prompt injection via retrieved documents (B) — malicious content embedded in indexed source documents (e.g. hidden instructions like 'ignore previous instructions and...') that the retrieval tool surfaces and the model acts on, and (2) context window stuffing (C) — submitting extremely long inputs to consume the context window, potentially crowding out retrieved context or causing unexpected model behaviour. SQL injection (A) applies only if the agent generates SQL queries from user input. XSS (D) is a web application vulnerability unrelated to LLM agent behaviour.

text: An Azure AI Foundry agent needs to access a SharePoint document library to retrieve policy documents as part of its retrieval pipeline. The SharePoint site uses Microsoft 365 authentication. Which approach correctly connects the agent to SharePoint content?
options: Configure a SharePoint connector in Azure AI Foundry — Foundry has a native SharePoint content source that syncs to the vector index automatically
Connect SharePoint directly as a data source in Azure AI Search using the SharePoint Online indexer, which handles Microsoft 365 authentication natively
Download SharePoint documents to Azure Blob Storage via Power Automate, then index Blob Storage as the vector index source
Use Microsoft Graph API as a function tool — the agent calls Graph API with a delegated or application token to retrieve SharePoint documents, then passes them as context
expl:
Correct answer: B — Azure AI Search SharePoint Online indexer.

Azure AI Search has a native SharePoint Online data source connector that authenticates to Microsoft 365 using app registration credentials, crawls document libraries, and populates the search index. This is the most architecturally clean solution — the vector index stays in sync without custom tooling. A native Foundry SharePoint connector (A) does not currently exist as a built-in feature. Microsoft Graph as a function tool (D) works but adds per-query API calls for content that could be indexed once. Power Automate sync (C) adds an unnecessary ETL layer and introduces sync lag.

text: A developer is using Azure AI Foundry to build a solution that generates short product descriptions from structured product data (JSON). The team wants to ensure that every generated description mentions the product name, key feature, and price — and never exceeds 50 words. Which technique most reliably enforces these structural constraints on GPT-4o outputs?
options: Use structured outputs (JSON mode or response_format with a schema) combined with a detailed system prompt specifying required fields and word limit
Lower temperature to 0 — deterministic outputs are more likely to follow instructions precisely
Fine-tune GPT-4o on 1,000 example product descriptions that follow the required format
Add a post-processing step that truncates all responses to 50 words and appends missing fields with placeholder values
expl:
Correct answer: A — Structured outputs with response_format schema + detailed system prompt.

Structured outputs (response_format with a JSON schema) enforce that the model returns specific fields, and a detailed system prompt with explicit constraints (required fields, max word count) provides the generation guidance. This combination is the most reliable enforcement mechanism. Temperature 0 (B) reduces randomness but does not enforce structural requirements. Fine-tuning (C) is expensive, requires retraining when requirements change, and is not necessary for a formatting task that prompt engineering handles well. Post-processing truncation (D) is a brittle fallback that corrupts valid sentences and doesn't enforce field presence.

text: The following code runs a Foundry agent evaluation using the Azure AI Evaluation SDK. The evaluate() call completes but the results dictionary is empty — no metric scores are returned. Identify the most likely bug.
code:
from azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, GroundednessEvaluator
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential

evaluator = GroundednessEvaluator(
    azure_ai_project={
        "subscription_id": sub_id,
        "resource_group_name": rg,
        "project_name": project
    },
    credential=DefaultAzureCredential()
)

results = evaluate(
    data="eval_dataset.jsonl",
    evaluators={"groundedness": evaluator},
    output_path="results.json"
)

print(results)
options: data="eval_dataset.jsonl" — the JSONL file is missing the 'context' field required by GroundednessEvaluator
evaluators={"groundedness": evaluator}
output_path="results.json"
credential=DefaultAzureCredential()
expl:
Correct answer: B — JSONL file missing the 'context' field.

GroundednessEvaluator requires each JSONL record to contain 'query', 'response', and 'context' fields. If 'context' is absent, the evaluator cannot measure whether the response is grounded in retrieved content — it either skips those records or returns null scores, resulting in an empty or incomplete results dict. The evaluators dict, output_path, and credential are all correctly configured. Always verify the JSONL schema matches each evaluator's required input columns.

text: A Foundry project team wants to ensure that when the underlying GPT-4o model is updated by Microsoft, their agent's behaviour does not change unexpectedly. Which deployment configuration prevents automatic model version updates?
options: Set the deployment to use a specific model version (e.g. gpt-4o-2024-11-20) rather than 'latest' — specific versions do not auto-update
Enable model version locking in the Foundry project settings — this prevents any model updates across all deployments
Deploy the model using a private endpoint — private endpoint deployments are excluded from automatic updates
Set update_policy='manual' on the Azure OpenAI model deployment resource in the Azure portal
expl:
Correct answer: A — Deploy a specific model version rather than 'latest'.

When creating an Azure OpenAI model deployment, specifying a fixed version (e.g. gpt-4o-2024-11-20) ensures the deployment uses that exact model version and does not auto-update when new versions are released. Deploying with 'latest' or a rolling version alias will update automatically. There is no project-level model locking setting (B). Private endpoints control network access, not model versioning (C). update_policy is not a valid Azure OpenAI deployment property (D).

text: A developer needs to implement conversation memory that summarises older messages to stay within the model's context window as conversations grow long. Which pattern implements this correctly in a Foundry agent?
options: Configure the agent's max_prompt_tokens parameter — the agent automatically summarises older messages when the limit is reached. This choice reflects one way to configure the solution in Azure.
Use Azure AI Search to store all messages and retrieve only the most recent 5 using a timestamp filter
Implement a summarisation step in the application layer: when message count exceeds a threshold, call the LLM to summarise older messages, replace them with the summary, and continue the thread
Increase the model deployment's max_tokens to 128K — a larger context window eliminates the need for summarisation. This option outlines a possible implementation detail for the AI solution.
expl:
Correct answer: C — Application-layer summarisation step.

Conversation memory management with summarisation must be implemented in the application layer. When the thread exceeds a message threshold, the application calls the LLM to generate a concise summary of older messages, creates a new synthetic message with the summary, and either trims the thread or starts a new one with the summary as context. max_prompt_tokens (A) truncates older messages but does not summarise them — information is lost. Using AI Search as a message store (B) retrieves by recency but misses context from omitted messages. Larger context windows (D) delay the problem but do not solve it for very long conversations.

text: In Azure AI Foundry, which identity is most appropriate for production services calling the project inference endpoint from an Azure-hosted backend?

Managed identity of the hosting service (e.g., Azure App Service or Container Apps)

text: A hospital triage agent assists nurses by summarising patient notes. Which TWO Responsible AI practices are most critical?
options: Human oversight and final decision by clinical staff
Data minimisation and HIPAA-aligned logging/retention
Disabling all logs to protect privacy
